companies.name: CoreWeave
companies.finMix: Asset-backed DDTLs (GPU-collateralized, incl. the $2.6B DDTL 5.5 for shorter contracts) + senior notes 9.0-9.75% + converts $10.8B (2031 at $107.80, 2032 at $119.60, 2033 at $97.85 — all out of the money) + OEM financing; total debt $46.9B at 30 Sep 2026 (recourse $41.6B, non-recourse $5.3B); 35M-share ATM open since mid-October 2026
companies.narrative: A GPU owner-operator running an essentially fully-contracted (~98% take-or-pay), hyperscaler-anchored book — Microsoft ~67% of revenue, plus Meta (~$21B), OpenAI (~$22B) and Anthropic, against a ~$99B backlog at ~5-yr weighted term. Near-term capacity is pre-sold and capacity-constrained, so the investable question isn’t whether it earns but what the back-half pipeline re-signs at, how fast it diversifies off Microsoft, and whether ~$23B of debt and $31–35B of FY26 capex can be carried while margins are still near breakeven. The target leans meaningfully on the path to 8 GW by 2030 — roughly a fifth of it rests on rumored capacity.
bull: ~98% take-or-pay book and ~$99B backlog de-risk near-term cash flows
Hyperscaler anchors (Microsoft, Meta, Anthropic) plus capacity-constrained demand

Capacity is sold before it is built and financed against signed contracts — each new GPU facility telegraphs a contract. companies.thesis: The market models CRWV's blended $/MW flat while its book re-signs up the Hopper→Blackwell→Vera Rubin ladder — the signed rate already runs ~$9.3M vs the $8M market dial, backlog is $99.4B, and NVIDIA contractually backstops unsold capacity through 2032. The argument has moved to the financing cost of that growth: the GPU-backed debt curve INVERTED in July, with the newest DDTL clearing at 10.44% (S+550/OID 97, 1.35x DSCR maintenance covenant) after pricing sub-6% in March. Q2 net interest expense is guided $650-730M against ~$21M of Q1 adjusted operating income.

calibration.appliesTo: the uncontracted share of each tranche only
calibration.basis: Ten reported quarters retrodicted with rampMult 1: MAPE 8.0%, bias -3.1%. There is no sell-down leg to calibrate — 98% of revenue is take-or-pay and bills on acceptance — so the observed lag between active power and revenue (the 2026Q1-Q2 additions bill over three quarters, >300 MW energised in June 2026 alone) is carried on the tranches directly as rampQtrs 2-3, not as a multiplier. Vintage rates were set so the retrodiction holds: $10.5m/$10m per active MW-yr on 2023-24, $9.5m on 2025, $10m on 2026.

ramp.basis: CoreWeave physical build-out model. 'Active power' and 'contracted power' as reported by the company are critical-IT MW (parity research 10 Sep 2026: the 10-Q lease note tracks Galaxy Helios's critical-IT figures 133/393/525 MW at every filing; the 424B4 counts Core Scientific at its 500/70 MW critical IT, not its 700-840 MW gross; the 4 Aug 2026 Indonesia release says '360 megawatts of contracted IT power'; no filing defines the term) — conversion to IT MW 1.0, range 0.9-1.0; gross is a site attribute (1.36-1.5x at Core Scientific and Galaxy), shown at 1.3x as a display assumption. History from company-reported active power (70 MW Dec-23, >360 Dec-24, 420/470/590/850 MW through 2025, >1 GW Mar-26, 1.5 GW Jun-26; 10-K FY25, 10-Q Q2-26, calls) and AI-cloud revenue by quarter; 2026H2 to the >1.85 GW year-end guide (11 Aug 2026); 2027 to the >3 GW active-by-YE27 framing on the Q2-26 call (Helios 393 MW undelivered, Applied Digital 225 MW, Lancaster, Kenilworth, Core Scientific Dalton/Marble/Muskogee, Chicago); 2028 most of the contracted footprint, the last 300 MW in 2029Q1 (10-Q Note 8: leases not yet commenced begin between 2026 and 2029); 2029 the >1.5 GW of options and LOIs, unsigned (ctr 0.9); 2030 the tracker's rumored pipeline (1.3 GW) — 7.0 GW at 2030Q4 against the company's >=8 GW objective, the gap left unmodelled. Research pricing is governed by data.researchPricing: existing/inferred book is held through its modeled term, same-hardware renewals retain the original all-in price, and new capacity uses one shared curve. Unmapped future power tranches from 2027Q1 use new-business assumptions; the legacy-book sensitivity retains the alternative inferred allocation. Sources for a power lease do not prove a customer compute contract. All expiry quarters currently remain estimates. Contracted and spot earning capacity ramp separately; no software attach is added above the all-in curve. The common curve, renewal continuation, generation factors and realized spot rates are house assumptions. Pre-policy reported-period calculations retain their historical calibration. These research valuations are separate from the broad asset engine.
ramp.actualsSource: AI-cloud revenue by quarter: 10-K FY25 and 10-Qs (2024 quarters from prior-year comparatives in the 2025 releases)

chain.fn: revenue = GPU-hours × (ctr × vintage rate + (1-ctr) × spot × gen multiplier)
chain.value: $10m per active MW-yr on the signed book (exit-2026 run-rate $18.5-19.5bn on >1.85 GW), $11.5m on 2027 vintages rising to $15m by 2030 (evidence-weighted base; the 14-17.5m ladder is the high case); spot $35m realised from 2027 on 10% of unsigned capacity
chain.assumption: Tenor, not generation, sets the price: the same Blackwell MW clears at $9.7-16.5m on 5-yr paper, $20-25m on 1-3 yr and $40-50m on 3-6 months, and 98% of CoreWeave revenue is 5-yr fixed take-or-pay, the cheapest tenor. Pricing is cost-plus to a target margin (mid-20s contribution, +5-10 pts on Q2-26 signings). Rubin earns more per GPU-hour but carries fewer GPUs per MW, so 5-yr Rubin paper per critical-IT MW ($10.8m at SemiAnalysis's $4.92 cost-plus floor; Nscale-Anthropic $12.4-16.3m depending on whether its 460 MW is rack or IT power) sits at or below late-2026 GB300 paper (~$14m). New-contract price at equal tenor and generation is at parity with IREN and Nebius within a +/-15-30% band; the per-MW gap is tenor mix (~90/10 5-yr/short here vs ~60/40 at IREN, ~50/50 at Nebius) and the locked 2025-26 book, not the megawatt.
chain.range: $10-21.5m per active MW-yr on 2027-30 vintages (research low $10/11/11.5/12m = $79/share; research high $13.5/16/18/19m = $157; owner parity thesis $12.5/19/20/21.5m = $177, see the 'parity' scenario). Open upward items from the 10 Sep critic: 5-6 yr Rubin prints at $7.4-8.0/GPU-hr (SemiAnalysis Jul-26, Nscale-Anthropic conventional reading) and Oracle-OpenAI would lift the 2028-30 rungs 10-30%.
chain.moves: ±$1m per MW-yr on 2027+ vintages ≈ ±$4bn of 2030 run-rate

companies.name: Nebius
companies.finMix: Prepayment + equity; convertibles; net cash
companies.narrative: A net-cash, prepayment-funded owner-operator that has flipped from spot-tilted scaler into a high-contracted, hyperscaler-anchored buildout. A ~$50B backlog (~92% Microsoft + Meta on ~5-year take-or-pay terms) sits over a smaller, fast-repricing enterprise tail — so ~half of realized revenue is enterprise (high revenue per MW, sub-1-yr), while ~80% of the contracted MW is locked to hyperscalers. Capital is structurally lighter than debt-heavy peers: ~$9.3B cash, low-coupon convertibles, ~$4.8B of customer prepayments funding ~90% of capex, plus a stake portfolio (ClickHouse ~$4.2B, Avride, Toloka, TripleTen) worth value outside the compute sites. The story is execution: only ~170 MW connected today against GW-scale owned campuses (Independence MO, Pennsylvania) that don't energize until late 2027+. Scale is modelled on its growth trajectory, not its (quieter) headline ambitions.
bull: Net cash plus ~$4.8B customer prepayments fund ~90% of capex — far less dilution/leverage risk than debt-heavy peers
~$50B backlog (~92% Microsoft + Meta, ~5yr take-or-pay) gives top-tier-credit, multi-year visibility
>75% of contracted power is owned (cheap Nordic / self-powered gas) — a structural cost-of-power edge
Hidden optionality in the stake portfolio (~$4.2B ClickHouse alone; IPO eyed ~2027) on top of compute
bear: Overwhelmingly a future-MW story: ~170 MW connected vs GW-scale targets — heavy back-end execution risk

Vineland NJ: the municipal hold cleared (Planning Board approved the ~588,000 sq ft Phase 2 site plan on 2026-08-17) but the NJDEP AIR PERMIT is still outstanding — the binding constraint moved, it did not go away
Two unnamed 'Pipeline 2030/2031 (growth)' rows carry 3,000MW and ~26% of site EV with no site, counterparty or schedule behind them
Convertible stack now ~$13.5B face and the August notes ACCRETE — the 2030s to 110% and the 2034s to 125%, a $5.8B claim on $5.0B raised
catalysts: Connected-power step-up through H2 2026 toward the 800MW-1GW year-end target
Microsoft (Vineland) ramping H2 2026; Meta firm compute from early 2027
Independence MO and Pennsylvania campus first-power (late 2027) proving the owned-GW model
ClickHouse IPO / stake monetization (Avride, Toloka) crystallizing the legacy value
risks: Permitting / interconnect slippage at owned campuses (Vineland NJDEP hold; gigawatt power timelines)
Capital intensity: the net-cash buffer erodes into a ~$20-25B capex plan, raising future financing needs
GPU-rate compression hits the fast-repricing enterprise tail and the discretionary $15B slice of the Meta deal
Stake marks are mostly undisclosed private valuations (only ClickHouse is primary-sourced)

basis.plannedRaise: NVIDIA $2B + ~$2.5B ATM + 1-2 follow-ons; prepayments fund ~60% of capex
basis.signedRate: 13.5 (was 11.5), owner-approved 2026-08-24. The old 11.5 was back-solved from the Sept-2025 Microsoft contract alone (~$11.6M/MW·yr) and had become a stale vintage average. Nebius's Q2 shareholder letter now discloses its own three-tier ACV ladder directly: 2026 INSTALLED BASE ~$12M/MW·yr, Q2 NEW SIGNINGS >$20M/MW·yr, Q3 SHORT-DURATION >$40M/MW·yr. Verbatim on the middle tier, stated twice independently: 'Deals saw an average yield of more than $20 million per megawatt' and 'The average TCV for these deals was greater than $1 billion, with annual contract value of $20-25 million per MW.' Blending the legacy book against the four 2Q deals — (17,400 x 11.6 + ~4,000 x 22.5) / 21,400 = $13.64M/MW·yr — supports 13.5 within 1%. Registry reconciliation holds: 13.5 vs the $11.60 $-weighted registry rate is a 16.4% gap, inside the 20% warn threshold. NOT set to 20: the >$20M figure describes MARGINAL 2Q signings, not the book, which is still dominated by the $32.3B Microsoft+Meta stack. The $40-50M/MW short-duration band is explicitly EXCLUDED — the letter frames it as 'a price opportunity in the $40-50 million per MW range and we signed our first one this week', i.e. N=1, price undisclosed, 3-6 month duration; a scarcity print, not a book rate [edgar 6-K 2026-08-12 EX-99.2 shareholder letter; sell-side GS 2026-08-24 corroborating]
basis.committedDebt: First senior secured debt facility, ~$775M, 6-K EX-99.1 dated 2026-07-17: matures 2030-10-31, priced SOFR+2.50%, MUFG-led and significantly oversubscribed, backed by deployed GPU infrastructure and contracted cash flows from an investment-grade customer whose contract is already in servicing phase; together with the customer cash flows it covers >100% of the capex on the underlying GPUs. Asset-level project debt per the house rule, so committedDebt not netDebt. Management frames it as 'a repeatable financing framework for more than $40 billion of additional customer commitments' — watch for a second facility at the 2026-08-12 print [edgar, company-ir]
basis.contractedPct: 85 — 2Q26: four landmark deals >$1B TCV each (Reflection, Cohere, an unnamed US AI neolab, a large US quant trading firm) added to the MSFT-anchored book; ARR $3.0B, exit ARR $7-9B reaffirmed; ~70% of 2Q deals carried customer prepayments (an all-time high) covering 50-60% of the associated capex; expected payback on Q2 deals cut to 1yr 10mo from a historical 2-3yr range. CONTRACTED-POWER TARGET RAISED 2026-08-12, confirmed verbatim in the shareholder letter: 'ending 2026 with 5 GW of contracted power, up from the +4 GW' indicated last quarter — the ladder runs >1GW Aug-25, >2.5GW Nov-25, >3GW Feb-26, >4GW May-26, 5GW now. UNIT FLAG: Nebius states contracted POWER (gross), not critical IT MW [edgar 6-K 2026-08-12 EX-99.2]
basis.netDebt: -9,038 as of 2026-06-30, rolled for the August convert. Balance sheet (6-K EX-99.1, 2026-08-12): cash and cash equivalents $8,042.1M + restricted cash $1,056.0M = $9,098.1M; Debt current $46.7M + Debt non-current $8,499.0M = $8,545.7M total debt, which is substantially all convertible notes and is carried OFF net debt under the house if-converted convention (the legacy converts sit in the FD share count instead). ROLL: + ~$4,940M net proceeds of the 2026-08-19 convertible offering (settled 2026-08-24) takes cash to ~$14,038M; the NEW notes are OUT OF THE MONEY (initial conversion prices ~$313.46 for the 2030s and ~$324.65 for the 2034s, struck off the $223.90 close of 2026-08-19) so their $5,000M principal STAYS AS DEBT and adds no shares. Net: 5,000 - 14,038 = -9,038. ACCRETION FLAG: these notes accrete to 110% (2030s) and 125% (2034s) of original principal, so the claim at maturity is $5,800M, not $5,000M, and both the redemption and fundamental-change repurchase prices are the accreted amount — netDebt carries principal per convention, with the $800M gap tracked as a watch item [edgar 6-K 2026-08-12; company pricing release 2026-08-19]

companies.thesis: Materially undervalued on our marks, but the gap is concentrated in unsigned capacity rather than the contracted book. Nebius's own Q2 disclosure repriced the story — new signings now yield $20-25M/MW against a ~$12M installed base, and contracted power guidance stepped to 5GW — while a $5.0B August convertible keeps the balance sheet in a ~$9B net-cash position. The swing factor is whether 3,000MW of unnamed placeholder pipeline is real and whether Nebius owns its economics at all under the new asset-light partnership model.

calibration.appliesTo: the uncontracted share of each tranche only
calibration.basis: Eight reported quarters retrodicted with rampMult 1: errors -1% to +20% from 2024Q4 on (the first quarter, 2024Q3, is a partial and misses by half). The lag between connected power and revenue is 6-12 weeks per management, carried as rampQtrs 2. Vintage rates were set so the retrodiction holds: $6m per MW-yr on the 2024 on-demand fleet, $9m on 2025, $12.5m on 2026.

ramp.basis: Nebius physical build-out model. Nebius reports contracted, connected and active power; active/connected MW are read as billing IT MW. History from the letters (~25 MW connected end-2024; ~170 MW active end-2025 against a 100 MW target; Microsoft Vineland tranches from Nov-25, the last large tranche landing December 2026; Finland 75 MW complete early 2026) and Nebius AI-cloud segment revenue by quarter; 2026H2 the guided step-up (800 MW–1 GW connected by year-end; UK 65 MW, Israel 80, Estonia 22, Bethune, Meta #1 clusters); 2027 the owned greenfields (Lappeenranta first halls with Meta #2 Vera Rubin from early 2027, Alabama, Independence MO phase 1 250 MW by Oct-27, Pennsylvania 250-300 MW by YE27, Bethune to 240, Vineland phase 2); 2028-30 the 5 GW contracted book online over 3-3.5 years (Q2-26 call), ~1 GW a year of owned campuses (Missouri to 1.1 GW by Dec-29, Pennsylvania ~300 MW/yr) — 4.7 GW at 2030Q4. Research pricing is governed by data.researchPricing: existing/inferred book is held through its modeled term, same-hardware renewals retain the original all-in price, and new capacity uses one shared curve. Unmapped future power tranches from 2027Q1 use new-business assumptions; the legacy-book sensitivity retains the alternative inferred allocation. Sources for a power lease do not prove a customer compute contract. All expiry quarters currently remain estimates. Contracted and spot earning capacity ramp separately; no software attach is added above the all-in curve. The common curve, renewal continuation, generation factors and realized spot rates are house assumptions. Pre-policy reported-period calculations retain their historical calibration. These research valuations are separate from the broad asset engine. Owned campus shell costs and the owned/leased mix remain company-specific. Rerun 10 Nov 2026 on SemiAnalysis’s 3Q26 site review and the company’s own statements: 2026–27 deliveries are re-phased one to two quarters later (Vineland’s third tranche December 2026, Alabama building 1 and Béthune’s next phase Q4-27, Pennsylvania mid-2028) and the 2028–30 wave follows one quarter later; management’s guide of 800 MW–1 GW connected by end-2026 is not met on this schedule.

notes: 5 GW contracted, >75% owned. Guidance stepped from >1 GW (Aug-25) to 5 GW (Aug-26) in a year. Owned greenfields: Mäntsälä and Lappeenranta (Finland, 455 MW), Independence MO (1.2 GW, groundbreaking May-26), Pennsylvania (1.2 GW, from 2027), Alabama. Leased: Vineland build-to-suit (Microsoft, 300 MW), Paris, Iceland, Kansas City, UK, Israel, Estonia, France, Spain.Q2-26 letter · 20-F · site releases

Connected lags contracted — and the 2026 guide is slipping. Management guides 800 MW–1 GW connected by end-2026 and more than 1 GW a year after. SemiAnalysis’s site work puts end-2026 at 573 MW and end-2027 at ~1.2 GW (cut from 1.7 GW): Vineland’s third tranche lands in December, Alabama’s first building and Béthune’s next phase in Q4-27, Pennsylvania in mid-2028. The page follows the later dates.Q2-26 call · SemiAnalysis 3Q26 update · AIB 8-K 30 Sep

Power is behind the meter at Vineland — and contested. Bloom Energy fuel cells (~250 MW guaranteed for 2026) and gas generators; New Jersey fined the landlord ~$1.07m on 22 September for 62 unpermitted engines with a permit deadline the landlord is challenging, and a 21 October Clean Air Act notice names Nebius. Phase 2, approved in August, lifts the campus to ~350 MW.Bloom partnership May-26 · NJDEP 22 Sep · notice of intent 21 Oct · Vineland Planning Board 18 Aug

~230k GPUs by December 2026 on ~490 MW energised — a quarter behind the company’s guide. Finland’s 75 MW hosts Europe’s first GB300 NVL72; Microsoft’s Vineland tranches are GB300.Q1-26 letter · Microsoft 6-K · model tranches
Five-year book life. Servers were depreciated over four years until Jan-26 (“conservative”), then five; the change cut H1-26 depreciation by $86m.20-F FY25 · Q2-26 6-K

Vera Rubin from early 2027. Meta’s $12bn dedicated capacity is one of the first large-scale Vera Rubin deployments, delivery H1-27; the $15bn backstop lets Nebius sell that capacity to others with Meta taking what is unsold.6-K 16 Mar 2026 · Q1-26 letter

Contract cohorts. Existing/inferred book keeps its original all-in rate until a disclosed or estimated expiry. Expiry ends signed coverage; continuation becomes an assumed renewal. New capacity uses one shared house curve.

Compare matching measures. Annualized earning contracted revenue divided by earning contracted IT MW measures contract yield. Total annualized revenue divided by all earning IT MW includes spot. Neither denominator should be paired with full energized-capacity ARR.

Evidence. Every tranche records price, commitment and expiry provenance. An inferred allocation is not a verified contract. New prices, zero software premium and 100% same-hardware renewal continuation are explicit assumptions.

Prepayments do the funding. ~70% of Q2-26 deals carried prepayments covering 50–60% of capex; >$9bn expected in 2026; Microsoft prepaid $6.96bn of $17.4bn. Deferred revenue $6.0bn at 30 June.Q2-26 letter · 20-F Note on Microsoft

Converts, then secured debt. Four convertible raises in 14 months — $1.0bn (Jun-25), $3.16bn (Sep-25), $4.34bn (Mar-26), $5.75bn (Aug-26); $13.4bn outstanding at original principal, accreting to $15.7bn, no capped calls — plus NVIDIA’s $2bn pre-funded warrant, a $1.15bn follow-on at $92.50 and $2.8bn of ATM at $223.60. The first secured GPU facility ($775m, SOFR+250) closed July-26; management expects “mid-single-digit billions” more against >$40bn of IG-backed contracts.6-Ks · 17 Jul 2026 release

The catch: prepayments and gearing follow signed contracts; the owned greenfields ($8m shell per MW) are built ahead of signing and most of the 2027 capacity is self-built. A $3.5bn 364-day Citi bridge was signed on 17 October. Unsigned capacity needs ~$19m of equity per MW, and new equity now prices near $134, not the $224 of the last ATM sales.funding stack above · 6-K 17 Oct 2026

Common calculation, different costs. The steady-state multiple is recomputed from horizon earned revenue per IT MW. Company margins, leased or owned shell costs, maintenance, tax and discount assumptions remain explicit.

Equipment life is separate. A contract expiry does not remove the GPUs or install a newer generation. Existing equipment renews at its own rate; the long-run maintenance reserve is a house assumption.
Reconciled value. Updated quarterly revenue passes through the existing debt, prepayment and dilution waterfall. The terminal multiple is recalculated from the displayed steady-state inputs.

Separate clocks. Pricing policy is dated 15 September 2026. The balance sheet is 30 June 2026 pro forma for the August converts — Q3 results arrive on 12 November 2026. Site timing and the market reference ($134.00, at which new equity is issued) are dated 10 November 2026.

companies.finMix: IF-CONVERTED: $594.4M 0.75% converts (2030, ~$14.86 conversion derived from 39.99M underlying shares, in the money, holder-convertible in Q4-26, stock-settled) counted in FD shares NOT netDebt; other debt $80.1M ($54.3M revolvers + $20.8M drawn on the Morgan Stanley $573M interim project facility at Riot DC Logistics LLC, non-recourse, stated maturity 12/31/26 + $5.0M note) vs $748.2M cash incl. $79.2M restricted -> ~$668M NET CASH at 9/30/26; Coinbase $200M BTC-backed loan repaid and terminated 9/21/26; AMD $180M term loan (SOFR+250 target) not yet closed; project debt still to raise: Rockdale bond after the investment-grade credit support signs, Corsicana $4.4-4.9B launching 2027 ($6.1-7.0B in all at 80-90% loan-to-cost); no ATM sales in 2026
companies.narrative: A Bitcoin miner that has become an AI data-center landlord on ~2.0 GW of owned, approved power (Rockdale ~700 MW and Corsicana 1.0 GW in Texas; Kentucky 300 MW mining). The contracted book is 1,151 critical IT MW on three leases: AMD at Rockdale (50 MW, 10-yr, ~$50M NOI/yr), Anthropic at Rockdale (191 MW, 20-yr, $9.1B initial-term revenue, $361-406M NOI/yr, Phase 1 rent Dec-2027) and Anthropic at Corsicana — a binding 15-year triple-net powered-land lease for 910 MW of critical IT on the full 1.0 GW (signed 10/28/26, effective 11/4/26): $130 per kW-month with 3% escalators, ~$28B of base rent, ~$1.8B average annual NOI at a ~99% margin, delivered in phases of 400 MW (Jun-Sep 2027), 200 MW (Jan 2028) and 310 MW (Jul 2028). Riot delivers land, power infrastructure and powered pads; the tenant buys, owns and runs the modules, and Riot reimburses up to $3.64B of module cost after each phase pays rent — $5.5B of Riot capital in all ($6M per IT MW), to be funded by $4.4-4.9B of non-recourse project debt launching in 2027 (if it cannot be raised, the tenant funds the modules and recovers them as rent credits at 12%). Capex on the three leases totals $7.7-7.9B against a Riot cash-equity need of $0.8-1.5B; the Bitcoin treasury has been sold down to 2,418 BTC to fund it and Corsicana mining ramps down from summer 2027. Anthropic is 96% of contracted MW.
bull: Three signed leases, 1,151 critical IT MW: ~$38B of contracted revenue and ~$2.2B of average annual NOI — Corsicana alone is ~$1.8B a year at a ~99% margin
Corsicana is capital-light for a 910 MW campus: $6M of Riot capital per IT MW ($5.5B) against $130 per kW-month rent with 3% escalators — the tenant owns and runs the modules
Execution has proof: AMD 25 MW delivered on time, the next 10 MW due in November 2026; the Rockdale Anthropic build is on its Dec-2027 / Jun-2028 dates
Owned, energized ERCOT power outside the batch process, with ~200-250 IT MW still leasable at Rockdale plus AMD's 150 MW of expansion rights
bear: One tenant is 96% of contracted MW; no guarantee, letter of credit or investment-grade backstop is disclosed for Corsicana and Rockdale's credit support is still unsigned
$7.7-7.9B of capex with $6.1-7.0B of non-recourse project debt still to raise in a tight credit market; the Morgan Stanley interim facility matures 12/31/26
If the Corsicana debt cannot be raised the tenant funds the modules and takes rent credits at 12% — net rent falls materially
Delivery risk is contractual: rent credits after 60 days late and a phase-level termination right after 270 days; first block due 28 June 2027
catalysts: Rockdale investment-grade credit support signed and permanent project financing replacing the Morgan Stanley facility (stated maturity 12/31/26)
Corsicana project financing ($4.4-4.9B, non-recourse) launching 2027
Corsicana Phase 1 first block 28 June 2027, full 400 MW 11 September 2027; Rockdale Anthropic Phase 1 rent December 2027
AMD term loan close ($180M), AMD Phase 3 (10 MW, November 2026) and the remaining 150 MW of AMD expansion rights; more Rockdale capacity for the existing tenant
risks: Counterparty concentration: Anthropic PBC is 1,101 of 1,151 contracted IT MW, with undisclosed credit support at Corsicana
Financing: $6.1-7.0B of project debt to place; failure shifts Corsicana to tenant-funded modules with 12% rent credits
Schedule: 910 MW of powered pads between June 2027 and July 2028, with late-delivery credits and phase termination rights

companies.narrative: A Bitcoin miner and ASIC designer pivoting into AI/HPC by converting power-rich crypto campuses to colocation, leasing capacity to AI tenants on landlord economics, alongside a small high-margin owner-operated GPU-cloud sleeve. The structural edge is owned cheap-to-mid power (Nordic hydro at Tydal, Columbia hydro at Wenatchee, ERCOT at Rockdale, TVA at Knoxville) and an unusually low ~6% blended cost of debt from a ~$1.4B cheap-convertible stack. Its flagship Tydal (Norway) campus has a signed colocation lease that is not yet effective — tenant unnamed, terms withheld. Beyond ~$69M of AI-cloud ARR, essentially nothing is firmly contracted: the GW-scale value drivers (Tydal, Clarington, Niles, Rockdale) are signed-but-conditional or in negotiation, so most modelled MW is owned and scheduled (high existence) but not yet leased. The question is execution — energizing the pipeline, clearing the Clarington litigation, and signing credible AI tenants while financing-funded cash burn and dilution continue.

ramp.basis: IREN physical build-out model: company-disclosed 480 MW gross 2026 program and 1,210 MW cumulative 2027 program. Horizon 1 was accepted by Microsoft in August 2026 and anchors first lease revenue in 2026Q3; Horizons 2–4, Mackenzie and the first Childress air-cooled halls are powered but bill from January–February 2027 after a Microsoft-requested network change and supplier delays (Q1 FY27 10-Q), so their first revenue is 2027Q1 while purchases stay on the committed calendar; the NVIDIA air-cooled block and the first 2027 retrofit follow one quarter later. Later tranches are schedules; 2028–30 extrapolate the modeled construction cadence. Nostrum first revenue is a permitting/construction inference for 2029Q3; Kiowa timing reflects the modeled power queue. Gross and IT capacity are distinct: the modeled IT conversion is toward the upper end of the rounded company disclosures and requires continued reconciliation. Microsoft and NVIDIA named contract allocations retain their inferred GPU-hour economics and disclosed five-year term; exact calendar expiries remain estimated. Research pricing is governed by data.researchPricing: existing/inferred book is held through its modeled term, same-hardware renewals retain the original all-in price, and new capacity uses one shared curve. Unmapped future power tranches from 2027Q1 use new-business assumptions; the legacy-book sensitivity retains the alternative inferred allocation. Sources for a power lease do not prove a customer compute contract. All expiry quarters currently remain estimates. Contracted and spot earning capacity ramp separately; no software attach is added above the all-in curve. The common curve, renewal continuation, generation factors and realized spot rates are house assumptions. Pre-policy reported-period calculations retain their historical calibration. These research valuations are separate from the broad asset engine.

chain.value: fleet-weighted Hopper 1.60 kW (627/IT-MW), Blackwell 2.48 kW (404), Rubin-class 4.23 kW (236), next-gen 6.30 kW (159) — but gpus is a STORED field per tranche, not derived, and the per-tranche spread is wide: Hopper 625–633/IT-MW, Blackwell 340–564 (that spread is COOLING, not noise: liquid GB300 NVL72 ~2.63 kW/GPU, air-cooled B200/B300 in converted shells ~1.77–2.20), Rubin 214–285, next-gen 158–159
chain.assumption: All-in at the IT boundary: accelerator + host CPU + memory + network + storage share, cooling already excluded by the derate. Anchored on IREN's disclosure of >19,000 GB300 per 50 MW-IT Horizon building (2.63 kW/GPU), which the Horizon tranches match exactly. THE LADDER IS PINNED TO SILICON, NOT TO TREND. Per-package accelerator TDP runs H100/H200 700 W → GB300 1,400 W → VR200 2,300 W (the raised VR200 spec reported Oct-2025, consistent with 72 packages in a 190–230 kW NVL72 rack), i.e. +100% then +64%; the modelled IT-boundary ladder steps +55% (Hopper→Blackwell) and +71% (Blackwell→Rubin), tracking the silicon to within 7 points. The next-gen rung is therefore set at 6.30 kW (+49% on Rubin), NOT the 4.91 kW (+16%) it previously carried: a +16% rung is supported by no roadmap point — Rubin Ultra alone puts 144 quad-die packages in a ~600 kW Kyber rack (4.17 kW/package at the rack boundary, +58% on VR200's 2.64–3.19) and the 2028 Feynman generation is briefed at ~2 kW per die in ~1 MW racks. HONEST CAVEAT: gpus is stored per tranche rather than derived from itMW, so this link DESCRIBES the data rather than generating it — the fleet averages above are outputs, and individual tranches sit up to 41% away from them. The density scenarios move the whole generation, so a tranche already at the top of its band (Sweetwater 1 initial is 285/IT-MW, above the +18% target) is pushed beyond it. DENSITY IS NOT A MONEY LEVER ON ITS OWN: revenue is IT-MW × $/kW-hr, so re-cutting next-gen from 4.91 to 6.30 kW moves the fleet headline (YE-30 748k → 724k live GPUs; next-gen nameplate 157,000 → 122,300) and leaves CY2030 revenue within 0.04% once the vintage rate is rebased with it. CROSS-PAGE NOTE (parity research 10 Sep 2026): this next-gen rung (6.30 kW, 159/IT-MW) is a Feynman-class reading one generation later than the CoreWeave and Nebius 'next' (Rubin Ultra NVL576, ~200/MW), so $/GPU-hr comparisons across the three pages on the last vintage are not like-for-like; revenue per IT MW is.

chain.assumption: Each vintage is a separate rate on a named tranche set, and only three of the nine come off a dated print. PRINTED. $2.91 — Horizon 1–4 (Microsoft GB300, 300 MW gross / 200 MW IT, 76,000 packages, first revenue 2026Q3–2027Q1): implied by the $9.7bn five-year contract in IREN's 8-K of 3-Nov-2025 and the ~$1.94bn annualised run-rate IREN attaches to it (1.94e9 ÷ (76,000 × 8,760) = $2.91). 8.9% of CY2030 revenue. $3.10 — NVIDIA 60 MW air Blackwell at Childress (25,000 packages, first revenue 2027Q1): the $3.4bn five-year contract announced 7-May-2026 carries ~$0.7bn ARR, which implies $3.20; the model runs 3% under the print. 3.1%. $2.48 — legacy H100/H200 and the Sep-2025 cohort: IREN's own disclosed ARR-implied rate (>$500m ARR on 23,000 GPUs). 1.2%. COMPARATOR, NOT OUR PRINT. $3.97 — Nebius/Microsoft, $17.4bn over five years on 100,000 GB300 (announced 8-Sep-2025, extended to $19.4bn Oct-2025). It bounds the GB300 vintage from above; IREN prints 27% below it. DERIVED, NO PRINT. $2.72 (Prince George / BC expansion) and $2.85 (50k B300, Mackenzie + Childress air) are the $2.91 GB300 print stepped for air-cooled, smaller-cluster and renewal terms — 6.2% of CY2030 revenue between them. $3.20 (Childress air retrofits 27a–c and the 2028 completion, 12.4%) and $3.70 (Horizon 5–6, 4.8%) are forward Blackwell vintages with no named counterparty and no signature. NO PRINT EXISTS FOR THE SILICON — RUBIN-CLASS AND LATER, 63.2% OF CY2030 REVENUE. $4.50 drives Sweetwater 1 initial and ramps a–c (900 MW gross, 159,000 packages, first revenue 2028Q1–2028Q4) = 26.1%. $4.60 drives Sweetwater 1 completion a–b, Sweetwater 2 phase 1, Kiowa phase 1, Bundey first halls and Nostrum first halls (1,200 MW gross, 186,000 packages, first revenue 2029Q2–2029Q4) = 26.2%. $6.40 drives the four 2030 waves (1,100 MW gross, 122,300 packages, first revenue 2030Q1–2030Q4) = 10.9%. As at 23-Jul-2026 nobody has disclosed a Rubin-class contract price: NVIDIA began VR200 production shipment to eight cloud partners (announced 27-Jun-2026), CoreWeave completed the first VR200 NVL72 rack validation on 1-Jun-2026 and booked initial Vera Rubin orders in its Q1-2026 quarter without disclosing price, and no official Rubin cloud rate card had been published as at Jun-2026. The $4.50–4.60 band is therefore a DERIVATION, and this is it: at IREN's own Rubin density of 4.23 kW/package it prices at $1.06–1.09 per kW-hr, i.e. 2–4% BELOW the $1.106/kW-hr the Microsoft GB300 print pays — a power-parity read, not a premium one. Cross-checks: $2.91 uplifted by the VR200/GB300 package power step (+64%) would be $4.78; the Nebius $3.97 comp plus the low end of the 30–50% first-availability premium the trade press expects on Blackwell NVL72 rates would be $5.16. Retail GB300 on-demand sits at $7.99–8.62/GPU-hr (July-2026), so five-year contract prints clear at 34–36% of on-demand; nothing in the model requires that ratio to hold for Rubin. The next-gen $6.40 is not a price observation at all — it is the Rubin $/kW-hr carried across the 6.30 kW next-gen package, so the density and rate links move together and neither is free. The blend rises on mix shift to costlier silicon plus vintage escalation, NOT price inflation on a fixed product.
chain.range: printed vintages ±0; Rubin-class $2.90–5.95/GPU-hr (no power premium at all, up to the Nebius GB300 comp plus the top of the 30–50% first-availability premium); next-gen $5.35–7.55 (0.85–1.20 $/kW-hr on a 6.30 kW package)
chain.moves: revenue directly, one-for-one. ±$1.00/GPU-hr on the Rubin band alone is ±$2.1bn on the $21.7bn CY2030 line (±9.8%) and ±9.2% on exit ARR; a 20% Rubin re-price down is −$1.9bn and −8.3%

calibration.appliesTo: the UNCONTRACTED share of each tranche only
calibration.basis: The commissioning ramp is the one link with an empirical test, and run uncalibrated the chain overstates every reported quarter (+41%, +90%, +64%; mean bias +65%). The correction is regime-aware, because two different things are being modelled: CONTRACTED GPUs bill take-or-pay from customer acceptance and reach full rate on the modelled ramp, whereas UNCONTRACTED capacity has to be SOLD DOWN, which is what the reported quarters actually measure — in 2025 only 11k of IREN's 23k GPUs were under contract. Fitting a single multiple on the uncontracted leg gives 4.4x and cuts mean absolute error to 11.0% with residuals −16%, +16%, −1%. A flat global multiple fits worse (14.1%) and has the wrong physics: it slows down take-or-pay contracts that bill on acceptance. The calibration is in the BASE case. Confound stated: the 23,000-GPU figure of Sep-2025 is announced-and-on-order, not installed-and-commissioned, so part of the miss is fleet timing rather than sell-down speed; both push revenue later and one multiple is the single-parameter expression of it.
calibration.residuals: −16%, +16%, −1% by quarter after calibration (11.0% mean absolute)

ramp.attachBasis: Storage, CPU, networking and managed-services revenue earned alongside GPU hours — NOT applied (0). IREN's contract pricing is quoted per IT megawatt on its ARR definition, which by the FY26 release footnote 'includes annualized revenue for storage and ancillaries', and Roberts credits 'what we attach on top in managed services' for the '>$20m per MW' figure; the $20.0M/IT-MW-yr the unsigned book is marked at is therefore already all-in, and an uplift on top double-counts (found by the Sep-2026 rate sweep, adopted 2026-09-02). The 5% previously carried was sized on CoreWeave's disclosure (storage + CPU + networking above $400M ARR against a ~$10.3bn run-rate, plus managed inference >=$250M by exit-2026) and remains the right order of magnitude for what the attach IS — it is simply inside the per-MW price, not additional to it. Signed tranches were never uplifted (their rates are back-solved from all-in contract dollars).

companies.narrative: A former Bitcoin miner (Iris Energy) that has made a genuine owner-operator pivot into AI cloud — the rare name here that OWNS and runs its own GPUs (NVIDIA GB300/B300, ~$5.8B Dell buy, ~150k GPUs installed or on order) rather than leasing space to tenants. It sells GPU-as-a-service from data centers it owns on cheap power: Childress TX (750MW campus, ~3c/kWh ERCOT) and 100% hydro British Columbia. The book is anchored by two top-tier 5-year managed-cloud contracts — Microsoft (~$9.7B, 200MW across Childress Horizon 1-4, 20% prepaid) and NVIDIA (~$3.4B, plus a $2.1B equity right) — ~$3.4B ARR contracted against a $4bn+ YE-26 ARR target (~$4.4B once NVIDIA commissions in early 2027), though live AI revenue is still small and the backlog is overwhelmingly future. The swing factor is a ~5.8 GW secured-power pipeline that dwarfs today's live base — Sweetwater TX (~2 GW) and Kiowa OK (1.6 GW), plus first international sites in Spain (Nostrum) and Australia (Bundey) — almost all uncontracted, so the book reads spot-tilted and the value hinges on lease-up. Most capacity operating today is still legacy Bitcoin mining being converted to AI. Legacy/non-core is small — a cash-positive but shrinking mining fleet, the Mirantis AI-cloud software stack (acquired in stock), and a ZERO Bitcoin treasury (mined coins sold daily), so no BTC-price bet. The crux: funding the ~5.8 GW build needs tens of billions on a small share base, so the model now charges that dilution explicitly (uncontracted capacity is raised as equity) — the per-share target is POST-dilution. The real question is whether IREN can contract and commission its pipeline faster than the equity raises dilute it.
bull: Rare owner-operator AI cloud anchored by two blue-chip 5yr contracts (Microsoft ~$9.7B + NVIDIA ~$3.4B) with a ten-name customer base behind them — ~$3.4B of the $4bn+ YE-26 ARR target contracted, near-zero counterparty risk, ~45% prepayment on new GPU capex
Massive owned, cheap, secured power (Childress 750MW + Sweetwater ~2GW + BC 160MW hydro) — the scarce AI input, mostly freehold
NVIDIA is a strategic partner and equity holder (right to 30M sh @ $70), aligning the GPU supplier to IREN's ramp
Low legacy/BTC risk: zero Bitcoin treasury (sells as mined) and a cash-positive mining fleet — value is core AI, not a BTC bet
bear: Backlog is overwhelmingly future: live AI-cloud revenue only ~$34M/qtr; even the ~$3.4B contracted ARR isn't revenue until GPUs commission — the ramp model has only ~60k of the 148k YE-26 GPUs earning at 31-Dec
The GW-scale prize (Sweetwater ~2GW) is largely uncontracted — power secured, but tenants/utilisation are not; big spec capex ahead of demand
Heavy dilution to fund a ~$20B+ buildout: $6B ATM headroom + ~$6.7B converts + rising GPU debt — the headline target is pre-dilution
Neocloud GPU rental rates down 60-75% from peak; uncontracted GPUs exposed to spot pricing and obsolescence
catalysts: Childress Horizon 1-4 (200MW, Microsoft) commissioning through YE2026 — converting contracted ARR into live revenue
First large Sweetwater anchor contract — the biggest re-rating event for the uncontracted GW pipeline
NVIDIA Blackwell commissioning (early 2027, ARR target to $4.4B) and NVIDIA exercising its $2.1B equity right
Hitting the $4bn+ YE2026 ARR / 150k-GPU milestone at ~85% contracted (vs ~74k deployed)
risks: Lease-up risk on the uncontracted Sweetwater GW — large spec capex with cloud demand TBD
GPU economics & obsolescence — spot rate decline, utilisation, depreciation on owned GPUs (an owner risk colos don't carry)
Financing / dilution — continued ATM issuance and convert dilution to fund the buildout

Contract cohorts. Existing/inferred book keeps its original all-in rate until a disclosed or estimated expiry. Expiry ends signed coverage; continuation becomes an assumed renewal. New capacity uses one shared house curve. IREN’s own prints now bracket the top of it: three-year $19–23m and five-year ~$17m per IT MW-year in the September quarter, then a five-year contract at ~$22m with 90% of the GPU cost prepaid and a short-term one at $40m.Q1 FY27 release · deck

Compare matching measures. Annualized earning contracted revenue divided by earning contracted IT MW measures contract yield. Total annualized revenue divided by all earning IT MW includes spot. Neither denominator should be paired with full energized-capacity ARR.

Evidence. Every tranche records price, commitment and expiry provenance. An inferred allocation is not a verified contract. New prices, zero software premium and 100% same-hardware renewal continuation are explicit assumptions.

“Recent customer prepayments represent 45–55% of GPU capex.” On Microsoft, prepayments plus $3.6bn of investment-grade debt funded ~96% of the GPUs. Backlog is $20.3bn across 15 customers, two-thirds investment-grade. The ATM has sold 29.6m shares since 30 June — 17.4m of them in October at ~$36 — and has $2.3bn left of $6bn.Q1 FY27 10-Q · release

“Our entire data center portfolio is unencumbered today, including Horizons One through four.” Lenders hold the GPUs ($1.49bn pledged, non-recourse) and the Microsoft receivables — not the land, buildings or substations.A. Lewis, CFO, FY26 call · 10-K Note 23

The catch: prepayments and 90% gearing exist only on signed capacity, and the FY27 capex guide has been cut from $25–30bn to ~$20bn — “purely and simply financial markets”. $6bn of the remaining $15bn is not yet funded. Unsigned capacity needs ~$25m of equity per IT MW, or is simply not built.CFO, 5 Nov call · funding stack above

Common calculation, different costs. The steady-state multiple is recomputed from horizon earned revenue per IT MW. Company margins, leased or owned shell costs, maintenance, tax and discount assumptions remain explicit.

Equipment life is separate. A contract expiry does not remove the GPUs or install a newer generation. Existing equipment renews at its own rate; the long-run maintenance reserve is a house assumption.

House default, 15 September 2026. Add 0.5× to the DCF-derived EV/revenue multiple for IREN. This is a valuation judgment, separate from operating cash-flow assumptions. The no-premium case remains available; other sensitivities are measured from the new default.

Reconciled value. Updated quarterly revenue passes through the existing debt, prepayment and dilution waterfall. The terminal multiple is recalculated from the displayed steady-state inputs, plus the separately disclosed 0.5× house premium.

Separate clocks. Pricing policy is dated 15 September 2026. The balance sheet is 30 September 2026, pro forma for October share sales and the 1 October term-loan draw. New equity is issued at the 10 November 2026 market reference, $19.73.

companies.narrative: Soluna is a renewable-powered colocation landlord, not a GPU cloud: it builds wind/solar-co-located data-center shells in Texas (plus a Kentucky site), hosts third-party Bitcoin miners who bring their own ASICs, and is pivoting the same powered-land model to AI/HPC. Today ~123 MW is operating (all Bitcoin hosting/prop-mining) and 83 MW (Kati 1) is energizing/under construction; the AI story rests on Project Kati 2 (Metrobloks JV, 350+ MW roadmap where Soluna contributes site/power/electrical and Metrobloks leads leasing to neocloud tenants) and Project Dorothy 3 (300+ MW, now backstopped by the April 2026 $53M Briscoe Wind Farm purchase giving owned generation and a power cost edge). The whole AI book is pre-tenant — a vertically integrated, cheap-power optionality bet on a tiny (~$220M), heavily diluting, going-concern-flagged balance sheet.
bull: Vertically integrated cheap renewable power — owns the 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm behind Dorothy, eliminating PPA reliance and creating a durable sub-4c/kWh cost edge for AI/HPC leasing
Real, scarce powered land in ERCOT with a 4.3 GW interconnection pipeline; Kati 2 (Metrobloks JV, 350+ MW) and Dorothy 3 (300+ MW) have site/power secured and the AI pivot is genuinely underway
Operating Bitcoin hosting book growing fast (data-hosting revenue +178% YoY in Q1'26) funds the platform while the AI campuses are built
Near net-cash today (~$41M net cash post-Briscoe) on a ~$220M market cap — large MW pipeline relative to enterprise value if even one AI campus leases up
bear: Zero signed AI/HPC tenants — the entire AI thesis is pre-lease; Kati 2 leasing is outsourced to JV partner Metrobloks and only ‘formal negotiations with at least one potential tenant’ have started
Severe dilution: shares +627% YoY to ~158M, a $500M ATM shelf open, warrants to Generate/YA — the model values the buildout on today’s shares but the equity to fund it isn’t subtracted
Going-concern stress: ~$79M LTM net loss, negative FCF, Altman Z ~-2.57, and ~$34M of 9% Series A preferred dividend arrears ahead of the common
Sub-scale and capital-starved versus AI-colo peers (Applied Digital, Crusoe, the larger miners) — needs huge third-party project capital that may price punitively or not arrive
catalysts: First signed AI/HPC anchor lease at Kati 2 or Dorothy 3 — the single biggest re-rating event; currently zero tenants
Kati 2 project-level financing close (top-tier AI-infra bank engaged) that funds the build without crushing common dilution
Kati 1 full energization + Dorothy 1B prop-mining consolidation lifting hosting EBITDA and proving execution
Dorothy 3 interconnection / power milestones converting the Briscoe-owned generation into shovel-ready AI capacity
risks: AI leasing never materializes and the spec shells stay Bitcoin-only at far lower revenue-per-MW
Equity/warrant dilution and a punitive ATM draw at sub-$2 swamp any per-share upside; Nasdaq listing/compliance risk
Preferred dividend arrears (~$34M) and project-level minority partners (Spring Lane, Navitas, Generate, Galaxy) siphon value before the common
Bitcoin price/difficulty downturn dries up the hosting cash flow that currently funds the platform mid-pivot

companies.narrative: Galaxy is a crypto financial-services franchise (trading, asset management ~$5B AUM + $3.2B staked, lending, ~$650M venture book) being repriced as an AI-infrastructure landlord on the strength of its Helios campus in Dickens County, west Texas. Helios is a converted Bitcoin-mining site leased to CoreWeave: 526 MW of critical IT load contracted across three phases (Phase I 133 MW delivered Apr 2026; Phase II 260 MW H1 2027; Phase III 133 MW) on a 15-year take-or-pay lease expected to generate >$1B average annual revenue at ~90% lease-level EBITDA margin. ERCOT has approved 1.6+ GW total (potential to ~2.5-3.5 GW), so most of the campus is approved-but-uncontracted optionality on top of the signed CoreWeave book.
bull: 526 MW critical IT load contracted to CoreWeave on a 15-year take-or-pay lease, >$1B avg annual revenue at ~90% lease-level EBITDA margin -- a long-duration, high-margin annuity.
1.6+ GW ERCOT-approved (campus potential ~2.5-3.5 GW) on owned freehold land in a cheap-power ERCOT/west-Texas basin -- scarce, energizable expansion optionality beyond the contracted book.
Funded with $1.4B project debt at 80% LTC plus $2.6B corporate cash/stablecoins and a cash-generative financial-services arm -- limited equity dilution; company is buying back stock.
Optionality of a second anchor or expanded CoreWeave deal across the ~1.1 GW of approved-but-uncontracted capacity could re-rate the campus.
bear: Single-tenant concentration: nearly the entire AI book is CoreWeave, itself a levered, unrated AI-cloud whose own demand/financing is the key dependency.
Most of the 1.6+ GW is approved but uncontracted -- value beyond 526 MW depends on leasing capacity that has no tenant yet.
Legacy crypto financial-services and treasury earnings are volatile and BTC/market-sensitive (Q1 2026 net loss $216M); segment value can swing materially.
Dual-class founder control and heavy notes-payable load ($3.1B) add governance and leverage risk during a multi-GW capex cycle.
catalysts: Phase I rent commencement and full 133 MW handover to CoreWeave (Q2 2026), then Phase II deliveries H1 2027.
A second anchor tenant or expanded CoreWeave lease across the ~1.1 GW approved-but-uncontracted capacity.
Energization milestones on the 830 MW ERCOT-approved expansion and progress toward the ~2.5-3.5 GW campus potential.
Investability re-rating as contracted lease cash flows season (potential tier lift toward IG/REIT).
risks: CoreWeave counterparty/financing stress would hit the entire contracted book given single-tenant concentration.
Construction, transformer/interconnection delays push out Phase II/III energization and the uncontracted expansion.
Crypto-market drawdown depresses the financial-services/treasury legacy value and overall liquidity.
Funding gap on the multi-GW buildout forces more debt or equity than modelled, increasing leverage/dilution.

companies.thesis: The 15-yr CoreWeave Helios lease (526 MW) is priced in at the WRONG level — the first primary print of Phase II economics (term-average NOI $2.42M/MW·yr, ~91% margin, 13.7% starting yield on cost, 3-5% escalators) runs ~29% above what we carried and corroborates the SemiAnalysis TCV tape. The option you are buying is ~0.83 GW gross / ~0.54 GW IT of approved, interconnected, unleased Helios capacity — a third of the '1.6 GW pipeline' framing — now with a second campus at McGregor TX behind it. Offsetting both: $3.5B of 9.875% project debt now sits ahead of the common.

Every incremental MAM dollar under the remaining ~$3.2B of the up-to-$5.0B program (headline $5.0B less $1,825.0M funded; corrected 2026-09-15 vs FY26 10-K) grows the floor by $1.80. Future contracts: the company’s stated policy is 10–20% of contract value as prepayment at signing, funding the GPU purchase order (10-K) — modelled at 20% of GPU capex on contracted capacity (~12% of contract value), credited evenly over the five-year term. Modeled future receipts retain the capex-based funding assumption; they are not secured financing. Inferred credits use modeled service start and contract expiry. steadyInputs.basis: Horizon revenue per earning IT MW and the actual modeled contract/spot revenue mix feed the shared steady-state DCF. Running costs at the 60% forecast margin (colocation rent, power, managed services and overhead inside it; no shell). A 55% refresh reserve every four years plus 3% annual spares on $53m of GPUs and ancillaries per IT MW (the filed commitments weighted across the five contracts; $48–56m per MW each) is a long-run house allowance, not compulsory retirement at a contract expiry. Tax 30% — the Australian statutory company rate for the operating subsidiaries (the FY25 10-K rate reconciliation shows Australia 3.6 points above the US 21% federal rate; the base-rate-entity 25% applies only below A$50m of turnover). Post-horizon market growth of 6% for five years is the shared house assumption on every page; it takes the 2030 horizon revenue of ~$18m per IT MW to ~$24m by 2035, above the shared curve’s flat $21m extension — holding it flat is worth −$29 a share and is an open owner ruling. New/renewed contracts reprice every five years in that terminal regime (the book is five-year paper).

DigiCo is named as a current host with no disclosed megawatts, and the former Visy paper mill at Ettamogah near Albury was bought on 16 September (price undisclosed, no development application, no megawatts) — an owned site outside the 212 MW.Q2-26 10-Q · FY25 10-K · 8-K 20 Aug · GreenSquareDC 19 Oct · ABC 16 Sep

The NVIDIA site lands in 2027. The amended and restated NEXTDC service order for 72 MW deploys in five phases from April to August 2027 and commits ~$623m over an undisclosed term; NEXTDC had 12 MW delivered and 60 MW of liquid-to-chip capacity under construction at M2 at 30 June. The company is “substantially dependent on NEXTDC”. NEXTDC’s 21 October update concerns M3, where Jemena suspended the 66 kV works in September and does not expect to recommence them before February 2027 (next grid increase FY2028; NEXTDC’s FY27 revenue guide cut to A$475–500m); Sharon’s M3 exposure is ~2 MW per Cantor, press-tier, and the update says nothing about M2.10-Q commitments note · NEXTDC FY26 report · NEXTDC ASX 21 Oct

Beyond 212 MW is not modelled. Management speaks of a “gigawatt-scale” ambition across Australia, New Zealand and Asia-Pacific and says capacity is only announced with a customer and financing in place; the page stops at the secured footprint, and the signed-book-only scenario stops at 120 MW.8-K 1 Oct 2026 · Q2 call

64,600 GPUs by 2027Q3 on the contracted book — 40,000 GB300 for NVIDIA, 8,208 B300 for ESDS, ~7,000 in New Zealand, 5,776 for the global technology company, 2,048 for the AI platform, ~2,500 merchant. The company says 68,000+ by mid-2027; NVIDIA’s 9 Sep 2026 Australia release names Sharon AI at up to 68,000.8-Ks · June deck · 1 Oct release

Short book lives, long contracts. The accounting policy depreciates computer equipment over two to five years (no GPU class, no stated residual); management describes a 3–5 year contract plus two or more years of residual life. The refresh reserve here is the house allowance used on every page, not the accounting life; full replacement at six years would take $2 a share off the base.FY25 10-K · Q1-26 deck

Density is the company’s own. 40,000 GB300 on 72 MW is 556 per MW (~1.8 kW all-in); the ESDS cluster 547 per MW; the global-tech clusters 481. No filing states kW per GPU. The house 400 per MW used on the other pages would put ~30% more megawatts behind the same GPUs.8-K 12 Jun · Service Order No. 1 · June deck

Contract cohorts. The signed book keeps its filed all-in rate until expiry: ESDS $3.52, the global technology company $3.75, the AI platform $4.16, New Zealand $4.31 per GPU-hour — $15.8–18.9m per IT MW-year; management guides ~$15m per MW including storage. New capacity uses the shared house curve. The company’s own measures: TCV over $8.8bn, and a 15 May 2026 guide of at least $470m exit-2026 revenue run-rate — which the page no longer reaches in Q4-26 (about $54m in the quarter, $217m annualised) because the ESDS cluster is ready for service only in December; the run-rate is there in Q1-27.8-Ks · Service Order No. 1 · Q1 call 15 May · 8-K 1 Oct

The NVIDIA block is a floor, not a price. Up to $4.88bn over six years on 40,000 GPUs is $2.32 per GPU-hour on average — NVIDIA’s maximum payment, which falls as capacity is sold to third parties; Sharon keeps the anchor price on capacity it sells and shares the spread above it at an undisclosed rate. The page carries $3.29 (owner ruling, 3 Aug 2026); the floor and a 40%-share placement are scenarios. No placement has printed, and reports of a pause in NVIDIA’s wider programme are unaddressed.8-K 12 Jun 2026 · NVIDIA Q2 FY27 10-Q · SemiAnalysis

Evidence. Contract dollars and terms are filed; the ESDS Service Order is public; GPU counts on two contracts are inferred; no customer is named except ESDS and NVIDIA. ESDS (CRISIL A-/Positive) says it paid a USD 140m cash advance; no letter of credit is disclosed. Its go-live has slipped from 16 September to December: cluster testing was still running on 2 November, with ready-for-service between the first week of December and 17 December. ESDS puts its price at ~$3.50 an hour against ~$7 now quoted for the same B300s. Of 13 tranches, 10 carry an estimated expiry, 6 an unverified price and 3 an assumed commitment; the 2028 Vera Rubin tranches use a house density (250 per MW) and a rate derived from the shared curve, with no company pricing.tranche table · ESDS call 2 Nov · CRISIL · GreenSquareDC 19 Oct

Prepay, then borrow against the contract. Policy is 10–20% of contract value at signing to fund the purchase order; the inaugural $356m GPU-backed SPV facility (Tranche A $150m at 7.25% stepping to 9.95%, Tranche B $206m at 9.95%, 42-month bullet with a cash sweep) is “the first in an expected series”, with Tranche A repaid from the escrowed customer deposit on acceptance. Its one-month availability period from 28 September has passed with no disclosure of a draw, extension or lapse; the net-cash tile is 30 June, and Q3 results come after the close on 16 November 2026.10-K · Q2 deck · 8-K 1 Oct 2026 and facility agreement

$2.6bn raised in ten months. $103m pre-IPO notes (converted at $12.53), $74m from the TCDC sale, $125m IPO at $30 (Feb), $350m 6.00% converts (May), $900m of equity and pre-funded warrants at $68.73 plus $700m 4.75% converts (June), $356m of GPU debt (Sep). The USD.AI ($500m) and Digital Alpha ($200m) facilities remain undocumented and undrawn.10-Q · 8-Ks · S-1/A 20 Aug

The catch: $6.1bn of hardware is committed on the contracted book against $1.86bn of cash. At today’s price the residual equity in the model is raised at $23.32, against a June placement at $68.73 (Situational Awareness now holds 21.1% at a ~$65 cost); the converts (strikes $48.24 and $99.66) stay debt unless the price recovers.funding stack · summary table · 13D/A 17 Sep

Costs are rent and power. SemiAnalysis’s inputs — colocation $100 per kW-month, power $0.05/kWh — leave 88–91% contract-level margins; the NEXTDC 72 MW order ($623m, establishment fees plus monthly charges, power passed through separately) implies $0.9–1.7m per MW-year depending on its undisclosed term, most consistent with a five-to-six-year billing term at $120–144 per kW-month; the company guides ~75% gross; consensus carries 47–50% EBITDA through the ramp quarters and 55% for 2027 once overhead and the NVIDIA share are charged. The page runs 60% in every quarter and in the terminal MW.SemiAnalysis · 10-Q · Bloomberg

Capex is $48–56m per MW on the filed commitments ($6.1bn on ~115 MW: NVIDIA ~$4bn for 72 MW including networking, storage and the VAST layer; New Zealand $765m for 14 MW; ESDS $720m for 15 MW) against a $39m per MW management guide. No shell: the landlord’s capital sits in the rent.10-Q · Q2 deck · Q1 call

Maintenance, not replacement. Tray swap at 55% of GPU cost every four years plus 3%/yr spares — the same house allowance as the other pages — on a five-year take-or-pay book that recovers the hardware inside the term at these rates (gross payback 2.1–2.9 years on the customer clusters, 4.9 at the NVIDIA floor).model · research pack

Some equity, not none. Base: 10% of the 2027–28 build plus whatever the prepayments, the GPU facilities and operating cash cannot cover, issued at $23.32 — the bridge shows the count. The June placement was at $68.73; the price has since fallen by more than half: $48 on 6 October to $23 on 23 October, with four days down more than 10% (8, 14, 16 and 22 October) around NEXTDC’s 19 October halt and 21 October M3 update, a 2× leveraged SHAZ ETF registered on 9 October, and no Sharon filing.8-K 17 Jun 2026 · stockanalysis · Finnhub

The NVIDIA economics are the swing. Floor versus placement moves the 72 MW block between $2.32 and $3.49 per GPU-hour; every $1 per GPU-hour on the block is ~$175m a year retained. The signed-book-only scenario shows what the 120 MW contracted today is worth on its own.scenarios · SemiAnalysis

Reconciled value. Quarterly revenue passes through the debt, prepayment and dilution waterfall; the terminal multiple is recalculated from the displayed steady-state inputs with no house premium. Both convert series are out of the money at the model’s own horizon price (reset-floor strikes $40.20 and $68.73) and stay debt. Pricing policy is dated 15 September 2026; disclosures and the market reference keep their own dates.model · 8-K/A 22 Jun · indentures

ramp.basis: Quarterly GPU-ramp overlay for Sharon AI (playbook §6e, tenant variant, drafted 2026-10-26 and reconciled to the research pack the same day) — DISPLAY ONLY. Capacity is leased colocation: NEXTDC 87 MW (M2 72 incl. the NVIDIA block, S6 10.75, M3 2, S3 2), GreenSquareDC SYD1 15 MW (120 months from a Sep-2026 RFS; online 19 Oct 2026), New Zealand 14 MW (commencement Q1 2027), other May-2026 providers ~16 MW, and 80 MW added 20 Aug 2026 with an unnamed partner: 212 MW secured, 120 MW contracted to customers. Every signed tranche carries the all-in $/GPU-hr that its filed contract dollars ÷ term ÷ GPUs ÷ 8,760 h imply: ESDS $1,264.2m/60 months/8,208 B300 = $3.52 (GPU line $3.30); global technology company $950m/5yr/5,776 GPUs (June deck) = $3.75; New Zealand AI lab $1.32bn/5yr/~7,000 (inferred) = $4.31; global AI platform $373m/5yr/2,048 B300 = $4.16; the NVIDIA block up to $4.88bn/6yr/40,000 GB300 = a $2.32 floor, carried at $3.29 per the owner’s 3 Aug 2026 ruling (expected third-party placement less NVIDIA’s share), with the floor as a scenario. Timing follows the filings and the counterparties: the first global-tech cluster accepted 20 Aug 2026 (Q3), its second phase and the ESDS cluster at GreenSquare SYD1 in Q4-26 (ESDS: go-live early November), the AI-platform and New Zealand contracts from Q1 2027, the NVIDIA 72 MW in five NEXTDC M2 phases Apr–Aug 2027 (10-Q amended service order, ~$623m over the term; CEO: full billing by Q3-27). The 92 MW of secured-but-uncontracted capacity is modelled energising 2027Q4–2028Q2 at the shared §6i curve, 90% contracted — a house assumption one to two quarters behind the CEO’s “212 MW deployed by end-2027”; the “signed book only” scenario removes it with its capex. Densities are the company’s own (GB300 556 per MW on the NVIDIA site, B300 547 at ESDS, 481 on the global-tech clusters, ~500 in New Zealand; Rubin at the house 250). Reported revenue before Q4-26 is sub-$2m a quarter; the calibration uses Q1-26 and Q2-26. Gross MW shown at 1.3× IT as a display assumption.
