leases.window: Nov 2026 – May 2027; signings run continuously rather than in windows, and the next sizeable one is most likely disclosed by 8-K or with Q4 results in late February
leases.site: Contracted power not yet active: over 4.6 GW contracted against over 1.7 GW active at 30 Sep 2026, about 2.9 GW by subtraction. In the tracker's rows the next blocks are Helios Ph2 (260 MW critical IT, lessor delivery guided to start in Q2 2027) and the Other contracted DCs 2027 block (230 MW, estimated)
leases.tenants: Expansions by existing customers lead. The Q3 release names Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, Cohere, Hippocratic AI, Jane Street, OpenAI and Perplexity as expanded relationships and Canva, Mirendil, Parallel Web Systems, Serve Robotics, Substack and Wayve as new customers; none is given a dollar value or MW
drivers: Revenue backlog stood at “approximately $132.5 billion as of September 30, 2026” against approximately $104 billion at 30 June: a net rise of about $28.5B in one quarter, or roughly $32B of gross additions after adding back the quarter's $3,661M of revenue (estimated) [edgar]
More than $25 billion of that was signed between 30 June and 11 August (prospectus supplement filed 2026-09-17), which leaves roughly $7B (estimated) for the seven weeks to 30 September [edgar]

Q3 “Grew total contracted power more than 900 MW to over 4.6 GW” while active power rose by more than 200 MW to over 1.7 GW; contracted power read about 3.1 GW in the Q4-25 release and about 3.7 GW at 30 Jun 2026 [edgar]

Deal shape is shortening: short-dated contracts are signed at about $40.0 million per megawatt of annualised revenue on three-to-six-month terms, and the $2.6B DDTL 5.5 finances contracts that average about three years, so the next signing may be smaller and shorter than the 2025–26 anchor deals [edgar]

Build-speed score held at 4.5: the year-end target of more than 1.85 GW active was restated on 10 Nov 2026 and the FY26 capex guide rose at the low end because infrastructure is being delivered sooner than planned [edgar]

leases.window: Nov 2026 – May 2027; contracts are being signed between prints, with two new ones and one expansion disclosed since 30 Sep 2026
leases.site: Capacity beyond the 0.3 GW (IT) programme now being delivered, inside the 0.8 GW year-end 2027 target: Childress Horizon 5-6 (100 MW; committed capex covers Horizons 1-6) and the first Sweetwater 1 data halls (200 MW initial, liquid-cooled construction underway), plus short-term air-cooled capacity at Childress and Mackenzie
leases.tenants: Existing customers expanding and new AI developers: the Leading Frontier AI Lab expanded its contract after quarter-end, and the $20.3B backlog sits with NVIDIA, Microsoft and 13 other customers. No filing names a counterparty for Sweetwater
drivers: Since 30 Sep 2026 IREN has signed a five-year contract at about $22 million per IT-MW with customer prepayment covering 90% of the associated GPU capex and a short-term contract at $40 million per IT-MW, and has “Expanded existing contract with Leading Frontier AI Lab” (Q1 FY27 release, 8-K furnished 2026-11-05) [edgar]
“Revenue backlog increased 22% sequentially to $20.3 billion” at 30 Sep 2026, and contracted pricing rose 11% on three-year and 12% on five-year deals [edgar]

Supply to sell: the stated target is 0.8GW of data center capacity by the end of calendar 2027 against the 0.3GW (IT) programme behind the ARR target, and Dell purchase orders of approximately $6.7 billion deliver GPUs in tranches from the second half of calendar 2027 [edgar]

The FY26 release described 2027 as “late-stage discussions with a range of new customers over a significant portion of capacity”; no 2027 anchor contract has been filed, so the range is set by AI-developer deals, not a Sweetwater anchor [edgar]

Build-speed score 4.0: Horizon 1 was accepted by Microsoft in August 2026, but capacity targeted for 31 Dec 2026 is now expected in the March 2027 quarter after a customer-requested design change, supply timing and third-party delays [edgar]

leases.window: Nov 2026 – May 2027; contract wins are reported every quarter and the next read is the 12 Nov 2026 print
leases.site: Capacity arriving from late 2026 through 2027 across colocation and owned sites; the next uncontracted owned block is Independence MO Ph1 (250 MW, under construction, company expects Missouri operational in 2027)
leases.tenants: AI labs and AI-native companies on one-to-three-year terms (Q2 named Reflection and Cohere, plus an unnamed US AI neolab and a US quantitative trading firm); Meta, which holds an up-to-$15 billion purchase commitment on upcoming clusters; Palantir commercial customers through the preferred sovereign AI partnership announced 8 Sep 2026
drivers: Signing is the run-rate. The Q2 letter (6-K 2026-08-12) reports “We closed four landmark deals for our AI cloud business, for an average total contract value (TCV) of more than $1 billion each, and a yield of $20-25 million per megawatt.” The named counterparties are Reflection and Cohere, plus a US-based AI neolab and a US-based quantitative trading firm [edgar]

Supply, not demand, sets the pace: “We could sell our entire 2027 capacity on these terms today.” The same letter says management is deliberately holding some capacity back for immediate customer needs, which caps how fast the contracted share rises even in a strong tape [edgar]

A standing backstop turns into contracts as clusters arrive. Under the 16 Mar 2026 agreement “Meta has committed to purchase additional available compute capacity across certain upcoming Nebius clusters up to a total of $15 billion over a five-year period.” Nebius intends to sell that capacity to third parties first, with the remainder bought by Meta [edgar]

Short-duration deals raise signing frequency: “In Q3, we closed our first short-term capacity deal.” The letter describes these as three-to-six-month contracts and sees a price opportunity of $40-50 million per MW [edgar]

The inventory to sign against is still growing: “We now anticipate ending 2026 with 5 GW of contracted power” (gross power secured by land and power commitments, not critical IT), and remaining performance obligations stood at $37,490.6M at 30 Jun 2026 [edgar]

Size is estimated, not disclosed: $1 billion of contract value at $20-25 million per MW-year over the one-to-three-year duration the letter gives for mid-term contracts is about 13-50 MW ($1,000M / ($25M x 3 years) = 13 MW; $1,000M / ($20M x 1 year) = 50 MW); a hyperscaler-length contract would sit at or above the top of the 15-100 MW range [edgar]

leases.window: Nov 2026 – May 2027; cloud service orders are signed on a rolling basis, while the first NC-2/NC-3 or NC-1 expansion colocation lease is in advanced discussion with no signing date given
leases.site: Likeliest next signing is a cloud order hosted in third-party capacity (the recent ones took 2.0–2.7 MW IT each in Sydney, Paris and Canada). The next colocation lease would be NC-2/NC-3 in Yadkin County NC (60 MW gross minimum, bought 28 Oct 2026, unleased, ready-for-service targeted late 2027) or expansion capacity at NC-1
leases.tenants: Colocation: the prospective customers behind the non-binding letters of intent, which include investment-grade counterparties and proposals with investment-grade credit support; Nscale, the sole NC-1 tenant, holds priority notification rights on future NC-1 capacity. Cloud: existing customers adding orders and new enterprise customers, as in the five that signed since August
drivers: “Signed more than $700 million of new Cloud Services contract value across five customers since the Company's August 2026 earnings call.” At that cadence another binding cloud order inside six months is the base case, and it carries most of the 85 [company-ir]

NC-2/NC-3 closed on 28 Oct 2026 for $60.0M cash. The company holds “non-binding letters of intent from a broad range of prospective customers for capacity at NC-2 and NC-3 and expansion capacity at NC-1” and calls the discussions advanced; these are letters of intent, not leases [edgar]

Spending is gated on a signature: “WhiteFiber's development spending plans are expected to be aligned with definitive customer agreements and financing.” With ready-for-service targeted for late 2027, a lease has to land by about spring 2027 for that date to hold; a binding colocation lease inside the window is put at about 40 [edgar]

On 21 Aug 2026 management's stated aim was to “execute long-term leases with high-quality customers for that capacity during the fourth quarter of 2026”. The 3 Nov and 10 Nov releases repeat the demand language but give no signing date [edgar]

Delivery record: “As of date of this report, the remaining 20 MW became operational, bringing all 40 MW of contracted IT capacity at NC-1 into operation.” Switchgear commissioning issues pushed the ramp past the August target, which leaves the build-speed score at 3.5 [edgar]

Capacity to commit is finite: working capital was $28.1M at 30 Sep 2026 and the 10-Q says existing resources “may not be sufficient to fund both this pipeline and our near-term debt maturities without accessing additional capital”, so new signings are paced to financing [edgar]

leases.window: Nov 2026 – May 2027; the Dorothy 3A lease is a closing deliverable due by 1 Dec 2026 (31 Dec 2026 at the latest), Kati 2 has no date
leases.site: Dorothy 3A, Briscoe County TX: 50 MW critical IT (about 75 MW gross) in a joint venture owned 51% by Applied Digital and 49% by Soluna, so 24.5 MW net; agreement signed 20 Oct 2026, not yet closed. Behind it, Kati 2 Phase I (100 MW critical IT, letter of intent with exclusivity since June 2026)
leases.tenants: ChronoScale Holdings (Nasdaq: CHRN), majority-owned by Applied Digital, under a non-binding letter of intent for Dorothy 3A. For Kati 2, one unnamed prospective tenant under a letter of intent
drivers: Soluna and Applied Digital signed a subscription agreement on 20 Oct 2026 “to form a jointly owned company to develop a planned 50 megawatt Critical I.T. data center for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing at Project Dorothy 3”. The documents to be signed at closing include “a data center lease between Tenant, as landlord, and ChronoScale or an affiliate thereof, as tenant” [edgar]

The lease is not binding yet: ChronoScale “has signed a non-binding letter of intent to lease the planned facility”, and “The lease remains subject to the negotiation and execution of definitive documentation, and there can be no assurance that a definitive lease will be entered into on the terms contemplated by the letter of intent, or at all.” [edgar]

Closing is expected on or before 1 Dec 2026, with automatic extensions for the county tax-abatement vote or title, “but in no event will the Outside Date extend beyond December 31, 2026”. The tenant is inside the partner's own group and Applied is already paying for site work, which is why the closing is put at about 70 [edgar]

Kati 2 adds a little: in Q2 the company “executed a letter of intent with a prospective tenant and commenced commercial lease negotiations”, with no lease reported since. Together the two give about 75 for at least one binding lease inside the window [edgar]

Build record: “Every phase of Project Kati 1 was delivered on time with infrastructure costs on budget.” The 83 MW site was completed in September 2026. That is bitcoin-hosting capacity, not an AI hall, so the build-speed score sits at 2.5 [edgar]

leases.window: Nov 2026 – May 2027; the likeliest signing is a GPU offtake on contracted Malaysian data-centre capacity, with a colocation lease on an owned site the much less likely branch (about 15%)
leases.site: Malaysia A901 (67 MW, delivery Q2 2027) and A202 (65.1 MW, Q3 2027) — data-centre agreements signed, customer offtake not yet disclosed; among owned sites, the 179 MW Rockdale TX load increase energising in phases from Q4 2026
leases.tenants: Unnamed AI-cloud customers on five-year offtake commitments with prepayments; Volta, the Tydal tenant, is the only disclosed colocation counterparty
drivers: Contracting is running ahead of delivery: the September update furnished 2026-10-19 reports “offtake commitments covering more than 70% of our ~21.7MW A201 data center in Johor Bahru, generating >$1.7 billion in expected revenue over 5 years and boosting total AI Cloud revenue backlog to ~$2.9 billion” [edgar]

Capacity without a disclosed customer contract is in hand: the Q3 release lists A901 as “Data services agreement signed securing 67 MW of capacity; GB300 platform. Full delivery planned for Q2 2027” and A202 at 65.1 MW for Q3 2027, neither with an offtake figure [edgar]

Offtake is the funding model, so management has reason to sign early: “Customer prepayments, together with project-level financing, are designed to fund AI capacity as it is contracted”, and Q3 operating cash flow was carried by “a US$263.8 million increase in deferred revenue primarily from customer advance payments for AI Cloud services” [edgar]

Owned-site colocation is less advanced: Rockdale is “In active evaluation of AI transition” with no tenant disclosed, and Clarington's timing “may be affected by ongoing legal proceedings filed by a neighboring company, American Heavy Plate Solutions, LLC” [edgar]

Build speed is mixed, hence 2.5: Tydal is reported on target, but Knoxville is 55 MW with “energization is now targeted for Q4 2027”, Wenatchee is H2 2028, and A102 is a Q1 2027 delivery against November 2026 in the August update [edgar]

leases.window: Nov 2026 – May 2027; the largest contracts were signed between March and August 2026 and none has been filed since
leases.site: The about 92 MW of the 212 MW secured AI Factory capacity that has no customer (first uncontracted tranche, 30 MW, for deployment by end of 2027)
leases.tenants: AI platforms, AI labs and technology companies on five-year take-or-pay terms, described by profile rather than name; third-party buyers of compute on the NVIDIA-supported 72 MW block also count
drivers: Inventory to sell is large: “Sharon AI has secured 212MW of AI Factory capacity, of which 120MW is contracted under multi-year take-or-pay agreements.” (release 20 Aug 2026), which leaves about 92 MW without a customer [edgar]

Cadence has paused: the five largest customer agreements were signed between 31 Mar and 4 Aug 2026 (ESDS, the global technology company, NVIDIA, the New Zealand AI lab and the AI platform). Of the latest, “The agreement has a total contract value of US$373 million over its five-year term.” No customer contract has been filed in the three months since [edgar]

The NVIDIA arrangement itself requires third-party sales: “The business model contemplates that we will sell all or part of this compute to Third Parties, generating a revenue share with such customer on the spread.” Any such sale is a new contract on capacity scheduled to deploy from April 2027 [edgar]

Funding limits how fast new orders can be taken: “Contractual purchase and infrastructure commitments make up the majority of the future spending and total approximately $6 billion as of June 30, 2026.” Cash at that date was approximately $1.86 billion and the first GPU facility is up to US$356,000,000 [edgar]

Size range of 4-15 MW follows the four third-party contracts on file (about 3.7 MW for the AI platform up to 15 MW for ESDS); prob 60 reflects five signings in five months followed by three months with none [edgar]

leases.window: Nov 2026 – May 2027; the company targets about $200 million of GPU Cloud ARR by calendar Q4 2026 and is about $15 million short
leases.site: Bell AI Fabric capacity in Canada — the Merritt BC Phase 2 option (7.6 MW in 2027, about 3,000 GPUs) and 3 MW of optional capacity in Manitoba; the owned Grand Falls NB site is still in design
leases.tenants: Enterprise and sovereign-AI buyers of dedicated GPU clusters on three- and five-year terms (the book holds Bell AI Fabric supporting Cohere and an unnamed investment-grade enterprise); ProCogia is procuring dedicated capacity under a partnership with no contract value disclosed
drivers: The target is still open: “HIVE is targeting approximately $200 million of GPU Cloud ARR by the fourth quarter of calendar 2026, subject to financing, market conditions, deployment schedules and customer acceptance.” Contracted ARR is approximately $185 million, so about $15 million of ARR is unsigned (estimated: 200 less 185) [edgar]

Signing record in 2026: about $30 million in February, about $225 million with Bell AI Fabric supporting Cohere in June and about $350 million with an investment-grade enterprise in August. On 27 Oct 2026 the CEO said “We have signed $600 million of TCV for GPU cloud deals this year, across 3 GPU off-take contracts.” Nothing has been announced since August beyond the ProCogia partnership [edgar]

Management's tone is defensive: “We recognize the macro headwinds in the AI infrastructure sector, and our primary objective is to protect our balance sheet and to maintain our cashflow and profitability.” Equity is also dearer — 751,937 ATM shares sold after quarter-end averaged $2.07 against $3.15 on the 13,698,085 sold in the six months to 30 Sep 2026 [edgar]

Capacity exists to land a contract: the 10-Q lists “British Columbia - Phase 2 (option): An additional 7.6 MW in 2027, supporting approximately 3,000 additional GPUs.” plus 3 MW of optional capacity in Manitoba [edgar]

Delivery record supports a build-speed score of 2.5: for the Manitoba B200 cluster, “Originally expected to come online in the quarter ending March 31, 2026, the units became operational in May 2026.” The GB300 cluster guided on 17 Aug 2026 for calendar Q4 is now expected in the first quarter of calendar 2027 [edgar]

Size range 1-5 MW: the two anchor contracts are about 2,000-2,300 GPUs each, carried by the tracker at 4-5 MW (inferred), and the $15 million ARR gap is about 1 MW at the book's rate (estimated) [edgar]

leases.window: Nov 2026 – May 2027; the 100 MW at Polaris Forge 2 has been in negotiation since the June 2026 deck and nothing has been signed since Delta Forge 2 on 5 June 2026
leases.site: The unleased 100 MW of critical IT inside the two 150 MW buildings under construction at Polaris Forge 2 (Harwood ND) — 200 MW of the 300 MW is leased; first capacity is guided for the second half of 2026 and full capacity for early 2027
leases.tenants: The investment-grade hyperscaler already at Polaris Forge 2, which holds a first right of refusal over the campus expansion; the tier-one investment-grade hyperscaler that took Delta Forge 1, Polaris Forge 3 and Delta Forge 2 in April–June 2026; the hyperscale customers in discussions on the Finland site are a 2028 story
drivers: The 10-Q filed 2026-10-07 states “Our two buildings at our Polaris Forge 2 campus, with an aggregate 300MW of capacity, are currently under construction” against a 200 MW lease there, so 100 MW is being built without a signed tenant and is due with the rest of the campus in early 2027 [edgar]

catalysts.title: Morgan Stanley $573M Rockdale interim facility reaches its 31 Dec 2026 maturity with the take-out not yet in place: an amendment extending it is the likely path

catalysts.title: Equity or equity-linked raise below the convertible conversion prices — degressive-issuance adjustment on both notes toward floors of $40.201 and $68.73 (negative)
drivers: The Q2 10-Q states “The Company is actively engaged in capital raising discussions with existing and prospective investors.” and lists equity issuances, debt facilities and hybrid instruments as possible sources [edgar]

Both indentures adjust for a degressive issuance — a sale of stock or equity-linked securities at an effective price below both the conversion price and the five-day average close — “in which case the Conversion Rate will be increased to an amount equal to $1,000 divided by the Weighted Average Issuance Price” [edgar]

The adjustment is bounded. For the 6.00% 2031 notes “In no event will the Conversion Price be less than $40.201 per share” (initial about $48.24); for the 4.75% 2032 notes “In no event will the Conversion Price be less than $68.73 per share” (initial about $99.66) [edgar]

Share effect at the floors (estimated: principal x maximum rate / 1,000, before accrued interest): about 8.7M shares on $350 million at 24.8750 against 7.3M at the initial 20.7292, and about 10.1M shares on $691.7 million at 14.5496 against 6.9M at the initial 10.0343 [edgar]

No modelled effect: equity issued inside the window is part of the tracker's planned raise, and both notes stay out of the money even at their floors with the shares at $23.32. Prob 35; priced about 50 because the shares already trade about 66% below the June placement price of $68.73 [finnhub]

No modelled effect: the tracker carries the ESDS site at December 2026, so a start inside the window changes nothing, and the downside branch (amendment, a shortened service period or termination on 15 MW) has no op. Prob 70 that service starts by January 2027; priced about 55 because the missed date is visible in filings but its consequence is not [edgar]

Prob 50 inside the window and priced about 35 — one US$356m facility at 9.95% is the only evidence of lender appetite so far [edgar]

catalysts.title: Dorothy 3A joint venture with Applied Digital closes and the ChronoScale data-center lease is signed (50 MW critical IT; Soluna 49%)

catalysts.title: Nasdaq minimum-bid deficiency notice (30th consecutive sub-$1.00 business day falls on 18 Nov 2026), opening a cure period to about mid-May 2027

The same 180 days from a notice in the week of 18 Nov 2026 would run to about 18 May 2027 (estimated) [edgar]

No Item 3.01 notice is on file as of 10 Nov 2026, and no reverse-split authority has been sought: the 16 Oct 2026 meeting voted on “(1) the election of three directors, (2) the approval of the Proposal to Increase Authorized Shares, (3) the approval of the Say-on-Pay Proposal, (4) the approval of the Auditor Ratification Proposal, (5) the approval of the Exchange Cap Proposal, and (6) the approval of the Adjournment Proposal” [edgar]

Prob 90: the price would have to nearly double to close at $1.00 before 18 Nov. It matters because the at-the-market program and the SEPA that fund the plan depend on the listing, and curing by price alone needs roughly a doubling inside the cure period; a share consolidation is the usual alternative. Priced about 60: the sub-$1 price is visible, the notice and its remedy are the increment [finnhub]

Precedent: the two May 2026 tranches were repaid, $20M on 24 Aug at maturity and $30M on 23 Sep after one 30-day extension. The lender is the 59.7% parent, so an extension is available if NC-1 funding slips and a default is remote; the 70 is for repayment on schedule [edgar]
Impact null: repayment swaps cash for debt. Priced about 50: the maturities sit in the subsequent-events note and resolve with the NC-1 funding the market is already watching [edgar]

catalysts.title: Cloud deployments enter service in their stated quarters: B300 orders in Q4 2026, Paris and Sydney in Q1 2027 (on the way to about $365M annualised by mid-2027)
drivers: “The Company expects its entire signed Cloud Services portfolio to generate approximately $365 million of annualized revenue at full deployment.” “That run rate is targeted for mid-2027, subject to equipment delivery, customer acceptance, data center availability and readiness, and securing required financing.” Q3 cloud revenue was $18.1M [company-ir]

Due in Q4 2026 per the 10-Q: 576 B300s in Iceland (five-year order), a 128-B300 order, two orders totalling 2,360 B300s for one new customer and a 1,024-B300 order (48 months). Due in Q1 2027: the Paris investment-grade customer, Sydney (about 1,200 B300s, 59 months) and a 2,048-B300 managed-services engagement [edgar]

Slip risk is documented. Paris is “now expected to commence in the first quarter of 2027, subject to final equipment delivery and acceptance milestones”, and its project financing is still in documentation: “certain material terms remain subject to ongoing negotiation between the parties”. In Sydney, “If service does not commence by the contractual long-stop date, the customer may terminate the service order and receive a refund of the prepayment.” [edgar]

“Remaining performance obligations under ASC 606 totaled approximately $729.0 million as of September 30, 2026.” The cloud share is $716.3M, with $12.1M scheduled for the rest of 2026 and $230.5M for 2027. Prob 50 is for every Q4-2026 and Q1-2027 start landing in its stated quarter [company-ir]

Impact null: the tracker values the cloud business inside legacy EV and no op changes it. Priced about 55: the run-rate target and the customer prepayments ($306.0M of deferred revenue) are public, but Paris has already moved and the schedule depends on financing not yet closed [edgar]

catalysts.title: Q4 / FY2026 results (estimated 25 Mar 2027): first print with all 40 MW of NC-1 billing
catalysts.window: late Mar 2027 (estimated from the FY2025 release on 26 Mar 2026)
drivers: Q3-26 base: “Total revenue was $24.0 million, an increase of 19% from $20.2 million in the third quarter of 2025.” Colocation was $5.6M with NC-1 contributing $1.1M [company-ir]

NC-1 status going into Q4: “As of date of this report, the remaining 20 MW became operational, bringing all 40 MW of contracted IT capacity at NC-1 into operation.” The first hall bills for the full quarter and the second from November [edgar]

Also due in the print: whether the Q4-2026 B300 deployments began on time, whether the NC-1 term loan funded, the status of the Bit Digital bridge, and any NC-2/NC-3 lease. The date is not announced; the FY2025 release was on 26 Mar 2026 [edgar]

catalysts.title: MTL-2 (Pointe-Claire, 5 MW gross, owned) construction starts
drivers: 10-Q filed 10 Nov 2026: “We expected to invest approximately $23.6 million to develop the site to Tier-3 standards with an initial load of 5 MW (gross). Construction is expected to begin during the fourth quarter of 2026.” [edgar]

The company's stated retrofit build time is about six months from the start of construction, which would put first power around mid-2027, in line with the tracker's row. No tenant is disclosed for the site [edgar]
Prob 60: a stated intention with seven weeks left in the quarter and no tenant disclosed, at a company whose capital is waiting on the NC-1 funding. Small in value terms; priced about 50 [edgar]

catalysts.title: NC-1 $300M term loan: the $200M initial loan funds (conditions: readiness and customer acceptance of the first 40 MW)
drivers: Signed 9 Nov 2026 with Morgan Stanley Senior Funding as agent: “The Credit Agreement provides for $300.0 million of term loan commitments, consisting of a $200.0 million initial term loan facility and a $100.0 million delayed-draw term loan facility.” “As of the date of this report, no loans had been funded under the Credit Agreement.” [edgar]

Timing: “Initial funding is scheduled to occur within 30 days after the Credit Agreement’s closing date, subject to up to two successive 30-day extensions under the Credit Agreement.” Counted from the 9 Nov signing that is about 9 Dec 2026, or early Feb 2027 with both extensions (estimated; the closing date is not separately stated) [edgar]

The company's own expectation: “Initial funding is expected later in November or in early December, subject to extension of the funding date as may be mutually agreed by the borrower and lenders, and remains subject to satisfaction of customary funding conditions.” [company-ir]

All 40 MW is operational and billing, but funding still needs customer acceptance, a mortgage on NC-1 and a completion guarantee from the operating partnership whose net-worth and liquidity tests are not final; the 10-Q adds there is no assurance funding occurs. Hence 80 rather than 95 [edgar]

No modelled effect: funding adds project debt and cash in equal measure, with proceeds reimbursing invested development equity after project costs, reserves and fees. Cost is Term SOFR (2.00% floor) plus 6.00%, with coverage and leverage covenants tested from the period ending 31 Mar 2027. Priced about 60: the signing came with the Q3 print, the cash has not arrived [edgar]

catalysts.title: First binding colocation lease for NC-2/NC-3 (Yadkin County NC, 60 MW gross minimum): letters of intent convert
drivers: The $60.0M cash purchase closed on 28 Oct 2026 and the sites are unleased. “WhiteFiber has received non-binding letters of intent from a broad range of prospective customers for capacity at NC-2 and NC-3 and expansion capacity at NC-1.” The proposals include investment-grade counterparties and investment-grade credit support [edgar]

“WhiteFiber is targeting initial ready-for-service capacity at NC-2 and NC-3 in late 2027, subject to customary development conditions.” With spending aligned to definitive customer agreements, hitting late 2027 needs a lease by about spring 2027 [edgar]
Management's August aim was to “execute long-term leases with high-quality customers for that capacity during the fourth quarter of 2026”. No lease is disclosed in the 10-Q filed 10 Nov 2026 [edgar]

Prob 40: advanced talks and a stated target, set against a letter-of-intent base rate, a balance sheet waiting on the NC-1 funding, and power that is a minimum subject to confirmation. Impact leases the tracker's 44 MW Yadkin row at the market anchor; an investment-grade tenant would be a quality step up from Nscale and Cerebras [edgar]
Priced about 30: the sites and the demand language are public, but no tenant, rent or term has been named and the August aim of signing in the fourth quarter of 2026 is not yet met [edgar]

v.CRWV: Tenant: every data centre is leased. 4.6 GW contracted and 1.7 GW active at 30 Sep 2026, more than 1.3 GW of the contracted power outside the US; landlords include Core Scientific (590 MW), Applied Digital (400 MW) and Galaxy (525 MW); more than 1.5 GW of powered land, options and LOIs sits behind the contracted book.
v.NBIS: Hybrid: 5 GW contracted guided for end-2026, more than 75% on owned campuses (Finland, Missouri 1.2 GW, Pennsylvania 1.2 GW, Alabama); build-to-suit for Microsoft in New Jersey; a partner model added in Q2-26.

factors.src: 10-K, NVIDIA release 7 May 2026 · 13G/A, release 1 Jun 2026, Q3-26 release · 13G, Q2-26 letter

factors: Three ways to reach the same megawatt. IREN buys the land and substation and waits for power; CoreWeave rents a finished hall and pays for it monthly for 7–16 years; Nebius does both. Everything downstream — silicon, contracts, customers, debt — is bought in the same market from the same vendors and lenders.sections 1–2 of each page
Evidence limits. Similar customer or hardware labels do not establish identical contract economics. Revenue per MW, term, prepayments and scope need a matching denominator and source.
economics: Like-for-like yields. Contracted revenue is divided by earning contracted IT MW; total revenue is divided by all earning IT MW. Energized capacity run-rate is not substituted into either measure.

Company economics. Ownership, rent, operating margins, capex and financing remain company-specific. Revenue multiples are recalculated from current modeled unit economics, not carried forward as fixed relative discounts.
picture: Separate confidence from value. Existing-book allocations may be inferred; assumed renewals and future contracts are separate categories. None is a probability-calibrated confidence measure.

Market comparison. All three reports carry the 10 November 2026 close as the market reference and as the price at which new equity is issued: $19.73 for IREN, $48.73 for CoreWeave, $134.00 for Nebius.

Balance-sheet dates. IREN and CoreWeave are on 30 September 2026 balance sheets (IREN pro forma for October; CoreWeave from the Q3 results release, with the 10-Q and its share count pending). Nebius is on 30 June 2026 pro forma for the August converts; its Q3 results are due 12 November 2026.
convergence: One market curve. New business uses the same house curve across all three companies. Term, hardware, cost, delivery and evidence differences remain visible. The initial curve does not calibrate a tenor premium or a company software premium.

Different books. Existing commitments retain their own original rates until expiry. Same-hardware renewals remain at those rates in the base case. No frontier-generation upgrade or price is granted to old GPUs for free.
Next evidence. Contract-to-tranche expiry mapping, comparable term-specific pricing and realized renewal outcomes can update the policy without redesigning the model.

footer.sources: The three research pages and their research packs (IREN Q1 FY27 10-Q, deck and 5 Nov 2026 call, and the FY26 10-K; CoreWeave Q3-26 results release of 10 Nov 2026, the 8-Ks of 17 and 22 Sep 2026, Q2-26 10-Q, FY25 10-K, 424B4 and the Q1-25 to Q2-26 transcripts; Nebius FY25 20-F, Q2-26 6-K, the 6-Ks to 17 Oct 2026 and the shareholder letters), lessor filings (Core Scientific, Applied Digital, Galaxy), SemiAnalysis public posts, index and “Neoclouds 3Q2026 Update”; the three-way convergence research round of 8 Sep 2026 (five strands, adversarially verified, filed at ~/Research/convergence-2026-09-08.json); the CoreWeave parity round of 10 Sep 2026 (four strands, two adversaries each, filed at ~/Research/CRWV/parity-2026-09-10.json).
footer.model: Recomputed from the same shared cohort, pricing and financing calculations as the company reports. IREN and CoreWeave are on 30 Sep 2026 balance sheets, Nebius on 30 Jun 2026 pro forma August; every reference price is the 10 Nov 2026 close.

mwBasis.IREN: critical IT MW, stated “(IT)” with gross given separately (gross/IT 1.4–1.6 liquid, ~1.2 air)
mwBasis.CRWV: active power = critical IT MW: the lease note tracks Galaxy’s critical-IT figures (133/393/525 MW), Core Scientific is counted at 500/70 MW critical IT, and the Aug-26 Indonesia release says “360 MW of contracted IT power”; gross 1.36–1.5× at its landlords
mwBasis.NBIS: active = IT by definition (20-F); connected is at most one PUE above IT (Finland ~1.1)

researchPricing.units: USD millions per IT MW per year; all-in contracted services
researchPricing.tenorBasis: The initial new-business curve has no calibrated tenor premium or discount. Term controls the next renewal date. A five-year, 15% lower-price case is an explicit sensitivity, not a disclosed market spread.
researchPricing.generationBasis: The shared frontier curve is quoted per IT MW, with generation factors of 1 as an explicit house assumption. It is not a hardware productivity forecast. Existing equipment renews at its own all-in price; renewal does not install new GPUs.

renewal.basis: Base assumes the same hardware keeps earning at the original all-in rate and 100% contracted capacity renews. These are house assumptions, not commitments. Price and retention downside cases are shown.

spot.note: Shared realized spot assumptions inherited from the CoreWeave/Nebius model, not executable rate cards. Physical GPU density remains tranche-specific.

researchPricing.basis: One shared new-business curve using the existing Nebius 2027–30 house ladder ($18m/$19m/$20m/$21m per IT MW-year). Prices fix at modeled service commencement, not energisation. Current disclosures support improving pricing but do not establish these forward prices. Existing/inferred commitments retain their own rates through disclosed or estimated expiry. No quantified company software premium is assumed. The 2031 service-start price holds the 2030 level flat; it is a house extension, not a market quote.
